approvals.note: Re-approved for registry-v2.0.0-candidate.3, covering #120 (the promotion guard gated analyte_key like a concrete definition, so every recognized-but-incomplete row was unacceptable). MEASUREMENT_RESOLVER_VERSION 9 -> 10 is the sole cause of the hash move from f00c0e6f...74efd1: candidateInputHash covers resolverVersion. No catalog entry changed - digestMeasurementRegistryManifest() is unchanged at 5341c12e8a38255a0276c92c98fdf8bc97adc3d85c916d0726347ea3983f7357. False-concrete resolutions: 0, unchanged. The safety question this scope exists for is whether any row gained a concrete identity it was not entitled to, and the answer is measurable rather than argued: running the corpus with and without the resolver change produces byte-identical report rows and identical thresholdChecks, and the same 8 rows reach a concrete identity through the same verbatim provenance as candidate.2. The resolver change narrows the ANALYTE tier to candidates that survived hard-conflict evaluation; it cannot widen concrete identity, which is still gated on `resolved` in both the resolver and the promotion primitive. Migration 046 relaxes only the analyte half of the incomplete-outcome guard; the resolved branch still requires both identity links plus a reviewed definition, and supabase/tests/writer_rpc_seam.sql asserts in both directions that an incomplete payload carrying a measurement definition key is still rejected.
